title: Purdue Online Writing Lab (OWL) Academic Writing Guide
evaluation: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5) — The Bible of Academic Writing & Rhetoric

thesis_statement_mastery.definition: A thesis statement tells the reader how you will interpret the significance of the subject matter under discussion. It is a road map for the paper.
core_characteristics: It makes an argumentative claim, not a factual statement.
It takes a stand rather than simply announcing a topic.
It is narrow and specific enough to be defended within the word limit.
It passes the 'So What?' and 'How and Why?' tests.

formula_frameworks.formula: Although [Opposing viewpoint / Concession], [Your argument / Thesis claim] because [Reason 1] and [Reason 2].
Because of [Root cause X], [Actor Y] must implement [Policy Z] in order to [Outcome W].

meal_plan.M: Main Idea (Topic sentence asserting a clear mini-claim)
meal_plan.E: Evidence (Data, research findings, citations, statistics, facts)
meal_plan.A: Analysis (Explaining *how* the evidence proves the main idea; unpack significance)
meal_plan.L: Link (Connecting back to the overarching thesis or bridging to the next paragraph)

exemplification: a salient case in point is

eliminating_wordiness.inflated: at the present point in time

passive_voice_calibration.good_passive: The participants were randomly assigned to two treatment groups. (Methodological objectivity)
passive_voice_calibration.weak_passive: Mistakes were made by researchers during the process. (Evasive hedging)
